name: relay-voip-node
description: RELAY mediasoup media-node agent. Runs ON a media node, NOT on the app fleet. Deliberately a separate package: the app is bundled with esbuild --packages=external and each app instance runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on every deploy, so a root mediasoup dependency would make every app box compile a C++ worker it never runs.
comment_entrypoint: `index.js`, not `agent.mjs`, and the name is a CONTRACT rather than a preference: infra provisions each media node with relay-voip-agent.service already enabled and held dormant by `ConditionPathExists=/opt/relay-voip/agent/index.js`. A different filename does not fail loudly — the condition simply never becomes true and the unit sits inactive forever, which reads exactly like a node nobody started. `"type": "module"` is what makes a .js file ESM here, so the extension change is cosmetic to Node.
comment_onlyBuiltDependencies: LOAD-BEARING, AND ITS ABSENCE FAILED SILENTLY. pnpm 10 blocks dependency lifecycle scripts by default, and mediasoup fetches/builds its worker BINARY from postinstall — so without this, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` here reports success, records `pendingBuilds: [mediasoup@3.19.3]`, ships NO mediasoup-worker, and the agent then dies in createWorker() at startup. Proven both ways in a scratch install: without it pnpm prints `Ignored build scripts: mediasoup@3.19.3` and finishes in 2.8s; with it the postinstall fetches a host-validated prebuilt worker and pendingBuilds is empty.
comment_pins: EXACT versions, not ranges. The two live nodes were installed at mediasoup 3.19.3; a fresh `pnpm install` against ^3.19.3 today resolves to 3.23.2, so the range alone meant a rebuilt node would silently differ from the running ones by four minor versions — and the worker is a HOST-SPECIFIC binary resolved per install (a prebuilt one validated against the host when a match exists, a source build otherwise), so nothing would surface the difference until a call behaved differently on one box. mediasoup's own API has moved inside that range (listenIps and announcedIp are @deprecated in favour of listenInfos and announcedAddress), which is exactly the kind of drift a range hides.
